title: Pot roast
subtitle: American chuck roast braised low and slow with vegetables
excerpt: A large chuck roast browned and then braised for 3 to 4 hours in beef stock, onion, carrot, celery, and herbs until the meat is fall-apart tender. The definitive American Sunday pot roast.
sourceNotes: American pot roast appears in Fannie Farmer's The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896, public domain), where it is described as 'pot-roasted' chuck or rump. It also appears in Joy of Cooking (1931) and in virtually every American home cooking reference of the twentieth century. The dish is descended from French braised beef and German Schmorbraten, adapted to American conditions and cuts.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool and freeze in the braising liquid. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Even better the next day. Cool, refrigerate in the braising liquid, and reheat gently for 30 minutes.

content.text: Pot roast is American low-and-slow braising at its most satisfying. A large, tough, collagen-rich chuck roast that would be inedibly chewy if cooked quickly becomes meltingly tender after 3 to 4 hours in a covered pot at low heat. The braising liquid reduces into a rich, savoury sauce. The vegetables cooked alongside are soft and full of flavour. It is a Sunday afternoon project that yields something extraordinary.

items.prepNote: bone-in or boneless chuck roast, or brisket
waxy, peeled, halved or quartered depending on size; add in the last hour

content.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 140°C). Pat the beef dry and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large, heavy casserole (Dutch oven) over high heat until smoking. Sear the beef on all sides, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deeply browned. Lift out and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic to the pot and cook for 5 minutes, stirring. Add the tinned tomatoes, Worcestershire sauce, stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Stir to combine.

Return the beef to the pot. The liquid should come about halfway up the meat. Bring to the boil, cover tightly, and transfer to the oven. Cook for 3 to 4 hours, turning the meat once or twice, until it is completely tender and falls apart when pressed with a fork.

Add the potatoes in the last hour of cooking. When everything is tender, lift the beef onto a board and rest for 20 minutes. Skim the fat from the braising liquid; reduce on the hob if you want a more concentrated sauce. Slice or shred the beef and serve with the vegetables and sauce.

items.symptom: Meat is still tough after 3 hours
items.cause: Chuck needs long, low cooking; temperature may be too high
items.fix: Ensure the oven is at 160°C, not higher. Check after 4 hours; some large cuts need 5 hours.

items.cause: Too much liquid, or not reduced
items.fix: Remove the beef and vegetables, bring the braising liquid to the boil, and reduce by half.

content.text: Pot roast is American Sunday food. It fills the house with a long, savoury smell and lands on the table at 3 pm. It varies by region. The New England version (Yankee pot roast) uses vinegar and sometimes turnips. The Midwestern version uses a cream-of-mushroom soup shortcut. The Texas version might include jalapeño and more Worcestershire. This recipe is the mainstream version, with no regional shortcuts.
